newsitem.title: THAILAND: Finance One denies rumours, clarifies position.
newsitem.headline: Finance One denies rumours, clarifies position.

text.p: Finance One, Thailand's leading finance firm, on Thursday denied it was facing a liquidity crunch.
Its shares fell the 10 percent daily limit on Wednesday on market talk it was facing problems meeting debt obligations.

"In response to widespread rumours that Finance One Public Company Ltd is facing financial difficulties, particularly with regards to our financial obligations to our Euro Convertible Bond holders and foreign exchange exposure, we would like to refute and deny these rumours," the company said in a statement issued to the Stock Exchange of Thailand.

"Currently the company is operating normally and regularly with no negative impacts from either our depositors and/or institutional creditors. We consider our liquidity in a very good position with strong deposits," said the statement, which was co-signed by President Pin Chakkaphak.
The company said it had never failed to honour debts.
"Finance One has never missed an interest payment on any bond issues," it said.
Finance One added that it had two outstanding Euro Convertible Debentures (ECDs). It has $100,000 outstanding on one, and $120 million on the other, which is due for redemption in 2001.
The firm also has subordinated debentures worth 2.4 billion baht ($93 million) outstanding, and due for redemption in 2001.
Finance One also denied that it was carrying foreign exchange losses.

"The present U.S. dollar appreciation against the baht has no material impact on the company's books because the majority of the company's foreign exchange exposure, including ECDs have been covered," the firm said.

The company said its investment portfolio was worth 27.84 billion baht, 5.56 billion of which was in listed equities. The company had made provisions to cover portfolio losses of 1.16 billion baht, measured against a SET Index value of 832.57, it said.
Finance One's net worth was 14 billion baht, the statement said.
Finance One denied that any senior investment banking staff had left the company.
